title: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’

author: Lauren Feiner
content_snippet:

title: SoftBank drops over 11% as Wall Street AI sell-off ripples across Asian tech names
title_en: SoftBank drops over 11% as Wall Street AI sell-off ripples across Asian tech names
author: Lee Ying Shan
content_snippet:
Asian technology stocks tumbled Wednesday, led by a rout in Japanese semiconductor stocks, as renewed concerns over the artificial intelligence trade rattles investors following an overnight sell-off on Wall Street.

Japanese semiconductor stocks tied to the global AI supply chain were among the hardest hit. Advantest, a supplier of chip testing equipment to Nvidia, plunged 12.26%. Tokyo Electron, which supplies chipmaking equipment to Nvidia's manufacturing partner TSMC, slumped 10.9%.

Technol
summary_en: Asian semiconductor stocks faced a rout following skepticism over ROI on AI capital expenditures and volatility in U.S. markets. Major suppliers including Tokyo Electron, Advantest, Samsung Electronics, and SK Hynix saw significant share price declines as AI accelerator demand confidence wavered.

title: Workday shares fall as soft subscription forecast overshadows third-quarter beat
title_en: Workday shares fall as soft subscription forecast overshadows third-quarter beat
author: Duncan Riley
content_snippet:
Shares of human resources and finance software company Workday Inc. fell more than 7% in late trading today after a softer-than-expected subscription revenue forecast for the current quarter overshadowed fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue that came in ahead of Wall Street’s targets.

For the quarter that ended on Oct. 31, Workday reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.82, up 22% from $2.32 in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $2.705 billion, up 11.2% year-over-year.
summary_en: Workday reported third-quarter adjusted EPS of $2.82 and revenue of $2.705 billion, both exceeding analyst targets. However, the stock fell over 7% due to a conservative subscription revenue outlook. CEO Aneel Bhusri emphasized AI product growth and the acquisition of ConductorOne to strengthen agentic automation.

Utah prosecutors dropped criminal charges against the prediction company Kalshi and its co-founders on Tuesday, one day after the company halted operations in the state. This is the latest — and perhaps most dramatic — victory for the states in their longstanding push to regulate prediction markets like gambling.

The move also undercuts the warnings Washington routinely issues to American companies and foreign governments about Beijing’s pursuit of US technology, they say.

content_snippet:
WASHINGTON — President Trump told The Post in an exclusive interview that he’s willing to pardon Jensen Huang if necessary — but that he believes the reinstalled Nvidia CEO should be fine without one and should “tell the truth” to Congress when he testifies next week.

summary_en: President Trump has publicly backed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO, advising him to speak truthfully in upcoming congressional hearings rather than invoking the Fifth Amendment. author: Peter Baker
content_snippet:
By his own account, President Trump was watching the stock market slide and decided to stop it. He would take it upon himself to determine who should lead one of the nation’s largest companies. Never mind national security concerns, never mind the autonomy of the private sector. Mr. Trump would decide.

The president’s extraordinary intervention resulted in Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as chief executive of Nvidia on Monday, just 11 days after he was forced out amid a Chinese espionage scandal.
summary_en: President Trump forced the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia after his 11-day ouster following allegations of ties to a Chinese intelligence asset. Despite warnings from intelligence agencies, Trump cited stock market stabilization as his primary motivation, sparking intense scrutiny in Washington over the intersection of critical tech leadership and national security.

content_snippet:
On the road that connects the villages to the north of Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank, there is always a watchtower and a gate, often flanked by Israeli soldiers with machine guns around their necks. Where drivers see a checkpoint, a barrier, and soldiers searching cars, the world’s most popular navigation app renders a clear blue line indicating the coast is clear.

content_snippet:
French and U.S. authorities suspect Iran was behind a cyberattack targeting supermarket refrigerators and freezers across Europe, an incident that reportedly spoiled food and caused equipment failures, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in damage. The attack affected about 700 supermarkets, raising concerns about the exposure of connected refrigeration systems and the potential for cyber operations to disrupt essential commercial infrastructure.

France’s Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot
